changes.before: Two texts contain the same number of words. Must they contain the same number of tokens?
changes.after: Tokens are the pieces used to represent text for a language model.

before: A language model learns patterns in language to predict or generate text. A token is one of the units used to represent that text.
A token can be a whole word, a piece of a word, punctuation, or other text. Word count and token count are not identical.
A tokenizer converts text into token identifiers. The exact split depends on the tokenizer and the text, including spaces and capitalization.
An identifier is a code for a token, not a score of how meaningful or true it is.
A sequence is an ordered list. Input text becomes input tokens; generated token sequences are converted back into text. This is a conceptual path, not an exact token trace for a named product.
after: A language model learns patterns used to predict or generate text. A token is one unit used to represent that text. It may be a word, part of a word, punctuation, or other text.
A tokenizer is the tool that turns text into tokens. The split depends on the tokenizer and the exact text, including spaces and capital letters.
A token identifier is a number used to identify a token. It is not a score for how meaningful or true that token is.
A sequence is an ordered list. Token order matters when forming text. Equal word counts do not guarantee equal token counts.

before.question: Two texts contain the same number of words. Must they contain the same number of tokens?
choices: No. Words can be split differently by the tokenizer.
Yes. One word always equals one token.
No. Token count tells you whether the text is true.
before.explanation: Token boundaries depend on text and encoding, not simply the number of words.

after.question: Two texts have the same number of words. Must they have the same number of tokens?
choices: No. Their words may split into different numbers of tokens.
Yes. Each word is always one token.
No. Token counts measure whether text is true.
after.explanation: A tokenizer can split words into smaller pieces. Counting words is not the same as counting tokens.
